name: Malformation Syndrome with Odontal and/or Periodontal Component
aliases: Congenital Odontal and Periodontal Malformation Syndrome

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Proposed Diagnostic Criteria for Malformation Syndrome with Odontal and/or Periodontal Component

criteria.description: Presence of congenital structural abnormalities of teeth including enamel hypoplasia or malformed crowns
Early-onset periodontal disease characterized by gingival inflammation and alveolar bone loss
Presence of craniofacial malformations such as maxillary hypoplasia or midface retrusion
Positive family history suggestive of autosomal dominant or recessive inheritance

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of both major criteria (congenital odontal malformations and early-onset periodontal disease) with or without minor/supportive criteria
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is clinical and supported by dental imaging and family history; genetic testing may assist but is not definitive.

pathognomonic.notes: Defective enamel formation leading to thin or pitted enamel
searchTerms: thin or missing tooth enamel from birth

pathognomonic.notes: Rapid periodontal attachment loss in childhood
Abnormal tooth shape and size present from birth

common.notes: Inflammation of gums often preceding periodontal destruction
Radiographic evidence of bone resorption around teeth
searchTerms: loss of jaw bone around teeth

common.notes: Teeth erupt later than typical developmental milestones
Underdevelopment of the middle facial skeleton

occasional.notes: Congenital absence of one or more teeth
Frequent infections due to periodontal tissue compromise

rare.notes: Bone infection due to periodontal disease complications
searchTerms: jaw bone infection secondary to other issues

rare.notes: Underdevelopment of salivary glands leading to xerostomia
searchTerms: reduced saliva production from gland hypoplasia

laboratory: Elevated inflammatory markers in gingival crevicular fluid
imaging: Panoramic dental X-rays showing alveolar bone loss
genetic: No specific gene identified; suspected autosomal dominant or recessive inheritance pattern
Genetic testing may show variants in genes related to tooth development
other: Clinical dental examination revealing enamel defects and periodontal pocketing

distinguishingFeatures: Severe periodontitis with early tooth loss
Premature loss of deciduous teeth without root resorption

redFlags: Rapid progression of periodontal destruction in childhood
Severe enamel hypoplasia leading to tooth fragility
Presence of craniofacial malformations with dental abnormalities
references: Orphanet: Malformation syndrome with odontal and/or periodontal component - ORPHA:139042
